lettuce irrigated with treated wastewater is contaminated with E. coli, and that the contamination is comparable to a laboratory experiment.

the contamination of lettuce from wastewater irrigation is dependent on irrigation method.

a risk assessment of E. coli contamination in lettuce irrigated with treated wastewater, and provides a basis for the development of a quantitative microbial risk assessment model for this crop and other salad vegetables irrigated with wastewater.
the risk associated with the consumption of lettuce irrigated in the field with domestic wastewater.
the development of a risk assessment model that will enable a more informed decision on the use of wastewater for irrigation of lettuce.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the laboratory method of submerging lettuce in wastewater is a suitable technique for assessing the contamination of lettuce irrigates with treated wastewater.
the microbial risk from the consumption of lettuce irrigated by wastewater is low.
the risk of lettuce contamination from irrigation with domestic wastewater is low and that the microbial quality of spray beds is comparable to drip beds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of submersion of produce in water as a laboratory surrogate to assess microbial quality of lettuce irrigated in the field is a valid method to assess microbial risk.
the microbial quality of spray beds was comparable to that of submersion of lettuces in wastewater of known concentrations.
the risk of E. coli infection from the consumption of spray irrigated lettuce is not greater than that of lettuce submersed in wastewater.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lettuce irrigated with treated domestic wastewater may not be a significant risk to public health.
the laboratory technique of submerging lettuce in wastewater of a known concentration can be applied to assess lettuce contamination in the field.
lettuce irrigated with municipal wastewater in spray beds is contaminated to a degree that would not be acceptable for consumption.
